sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 19.06.2023 at about 5.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-W-8358 on Sathanur - Achalu road, Kanakapura Taluk, at that time, driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MP-7971 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5269/2023 after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt.,
Hospital, Kanakapura, for after first aid, then shifted to Chandramma Dayananda Sagara Hospital, Harohalli, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient undergone surgery and spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards transportation, food, nourishment, medical expenses and other incidental charges.
Further he has to spent Rs.1,00,000/- for his future medication.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and doing Agriculture work and also doing milk vending work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

The accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MP-7971, hence, Sathanur Police have registered a criminal case in their crime No.99/2023 under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC against the driver of said vehicle.
The first respondent being the RC owner and the second respondent being the Insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MP-7971 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner constrained to file a petition.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further respondent denies all the allegations made in the petition.
Further contended that, the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further this respondent admitted the issuance of Insurance policy in respect of the vehicle Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MP-7971 and restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further contended that, driver of the vehicle has not valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5269/2023 petition averments in toto and also denied the manner of accident.

Further contended that, due to the sole negligence of the petitioner, the alleged accident occurred,
as the Petitioner had not posses valid D.L. Insurance to his vehicle and also not wear proper head gear at the time of accident.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for dismiss the claim petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 19.06.2023 at about 5.00 p.m, NH- 948, near Dyavegowdananagoddi village, Swathanooru hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing registration No. KA-01- MP-7971 by its driver as alleged in the petition?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If, so, to what amount and from whom?

In all they got marked Ex.P.1 to 16 (Ex.P.16 marked twice).
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led its side evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.

Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

8. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 19.06.2023 at about 5.00 pm., when he was riding a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42/W-8358 on Sathanur - Achalu road, Kanakapura Taluk,
at that time, driver of Car bearing (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.5269/2023 Reg.No.KA-01/MP-7971 drove Ravi vs Shankar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25375426/

As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief- examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

He has also got marked FIR and Complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, chargesheet, discharge summaries, NCS report, MRI report & Neurology report, OPD records, medical bills, Aadhar card, PAN card, CT Scan, MRI scan and medical bills at Ex.P1 to 13 and Ex.P.16.

I have perused Ex-P1 to Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.5.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 19.06.2023 at around 5.00 pm., and the FIR in crime No.99/2023 came to be registered on 20.06.2023 at 12.20 at Sathanoor Police Station for the offences punishable u/s. 279,
337 of IPC.
Wife of petitioner herein has lodged the complaint.

damages caused to the vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MP- 7971 (MV) like engine bonnet, front bumper,
right side head light and indicator, front right side wheel assembly, front right rear view mirror,
front suspension, rear left side door, front right side door and front right side fender damaged and to the vehicle bearing No.KA-42-W-8358 (M/C with gear) like front wheel dislocated, front suspension, head light and indicator, handle bar, fuel tank, crash guard, both side body, rear both side body, speedo meter, all foot rest, chassis, seat and silencer damaged.

11.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5269/2023 specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that, due to the negligence of petitioner himself, the alleged accident got occurred.
PW.1 denied the same.
Further the respondent No.2 put a suggestion that, at Ex.P.6 it has mentioned that, petitioner was influence of alcohol.
On perusal of the Ex.P.6 - wound certificate it has mentioned as 'patient was under the influence of alcohol'.
But petitioner has denied the same.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.5 filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5269/2023 all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-01-MP-7971 which belongs to the Owner/respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
let me discuss one by one:

a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: PW.1 has contended that due to the accident he sustained following injuries:
i) Right distal femur with sciatic nerve.

ii) Palsy right olecranon.
iii) Left lateral condyle of tibia.

(SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.5269/2023 iv) Right sacro-iliac joint.
In order to prove injuries caused to him, PW.1 has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.4 which also reveals that petitioner sustained above said injuries and the Doctor opined that, injuries are grievous in nature.

The record shows that, immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt., Hospital,
Kanakapura, for after first aid, then shifted to Chandramma Dayananda Sagara Hospital, Harohalli and underwent surgery and sustained severe sensory motor axonal polyneuropothy of right lower limb.
Petitioner examined Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW.2 and Dr.Sreedhara.K.C as PW.3 and they have assessed disability of the petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.80,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5269/2023 claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
PW.1 has produced 71 medical bills marked at Ex.P.10 which amounts to Rs.66,580/- and also produced 4 medical bills marked at Ex.P.16 which amounts to Rs.5,250/-.
On perusal of those medical bills at Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.16, it amount to Rs.71,830/-.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.71,830/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.
c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
Petitioner has produced 3 discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.6.

On perusal of the same, on perusal of first discharge summary, petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 20.06.2023 to 10.07.2023 i.e.,
for 21 days, on second discharge summary from 13.07.2023 to 19.07.2023 i.e., for 7 days and on Ravi vs Shankar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25375426/

going through third discharge summary petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 05.10.2023 to 10.10.2023 i.e., for 6 days in all for 34 days at CDSIMER Hospital.
The petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 34 days and as the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient totally for 3 times therefore, by including towards conveyance a sum of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment,
conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment: PW.1 has contended that he was an agriculturist and milk vendor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income.
Therefore, in the absence of positive documents regarding his income, this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2023 at 16,000/- p.m., Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2023 treated as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given &
duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5269/2023 petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 6 months.
Thus, by taking into account the notional income of PW.1, this Tribunal awards Rs.96,000/- (16,000/- X 6) towards loss of income during treatment period.

Further on third time admission on 05.10.2023 it has diagnosed uniting fracture of right distal femur with PFN in situ for physiotherapy and for follow up of right sciatic nerve palsy with foot drop and treated conservatively.

On going through the evidence and cross examination of PW.2 and PW.3 it is clear that, petitioner sustained right distal femur with sciatic nerve, palsy right Olecranon, left lateral (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.5269/2023 condyle of tibia and right sacro Illiac joint.

By considering the age, nature of injuries and treatment and also by considering the avocation of the petitioner, this court comes to the conclusion that, petitioner sustained whole disability in all at 28%.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 01.01.1995 and as on date of accident he was aged about 28 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 28 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "17" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
16,000 x 12 x 17 x 28% = Rs.9,13,920/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.9,13,920/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities: PW.3 has (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.5269/2023 stated that, on examination petitioner complaints of right lower limb weakness, difficulty in walking, depending on walker, bowel and bladder intact and presently petitioner is not working.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.

g) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 has stated that petitioner has to undergo 3 more operations like 1) Corrective operation for rectification of partial union of fracture of shaft of distal 1/3rd of right femur.
2) Implants removal from right Olecranon and 3) Nerve grafting (nerve transplant surgery) for foot drop (Common peroneal nerve paralysis).
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.

Regarding Liability: As discussed supra at Issue No.1, driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-01-MP- 7971 is liable to cause the alleged accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-01- MP-7971 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation of (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.5269/2023 .12,91,750/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .12,91,750/- (Rupees twelve lakhs ninety one thousand seven hundred and fifty only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.

going through third discharge summary petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 05.10.2023 to 10.10.2023 i.e., for 6 days in all for 34 days at CDSIMER Hospital.
Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 34 days and as the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient totally for 3 times therefore, by including towards conveyance a sum of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment,
conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment: PW.1 has contended that he was an agriculturist and milk vendor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2023 at 16,000/- p.m., Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2023 treated as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given &
duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5269/2023 petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 6 months.
By considering the age, nature of injuries and treatment and also by considering the avocation of the petitioner, this court comes to the conclusion that, petitioner sustained whole disability in all at 28%.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 01.01.1995 and as on date of accident he was aged about 28 years.
Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 28 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "17" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-01- MP-7971 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
